Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by logging each intake document with a reference number, date, and source account, then storing the entry in a dated ledger entry that links the submitted form to the originating identity record.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a ticketing platform account using a valid payment method on a date field that was recorded but not independently verified. The actor viewed the digital ticket barcode on a device screen; the authentication status of that display remained unverified. The actor captured the barcode image; the source file hash was recorded but its integrity check stayed unverified. The actor applied image-scaling operations to the captured barcode; the original-to-copy provenance field was left unverified. The actor generated multiple rendered copies of the modified barcode; the uniqueness check on each generated file stayed unverified. The actor transferred the copies to a secondary account; the transfer-authorization sign-off remained unverified. The actor listed the copies for sale on a marketplace channel; the seller-identity verification field was unverified. The actor negotiated a price with a buyer on a messaging channel; the buyer-identity check stayed unverified. The actor instructed the buyer to present the copy before the original; the gate-scanning log for that presentation remained unverified. The actor disabled notification settings on the ticketing account; the account-activity alert status stayed unverified. The actor declined a refund inquiry from the issuer; the refund-claim record remained unverified. The actor disputed a chargeback notice; the dispute-resolution outcome field stayed unverified. The actor deleted the secondary account after sale completion; the account-deletion confirmation log was unverified.

3) Materials/access observed: A mobile device with a camera application, an image-editing tool with scaling and cropping functions, a ticketing platform account, a marketplace listing page, a messaging channel, a payment method on file, and a refund/chargeback dispute form.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple rendered barcode images sharing a common provenance hash, a secondary account created shortly before the listing, a gate-scanning log showing an unknown identifier before the valid one, a disabled alert flag on the primary account, a refunded-then-reversed transaction pair, and a deleted account with no deletion-confirmation record.
